excerpts.text: From 2021 to 2024, Australia’s population increased from 25.7 million to 27.2 million, reflecting a 5.9% increase. Net overseas migration contributed 1.17 million people (78% of total growth), with natural increase accounting for the remaining 335,000.

Melbourne recorded the largest absolute increase in population, growing by 375,386 people (7.5%) to reach 5.35 million. Melbourne’s figures for net overseas migration (329,829) and natural increase (84,266) were both very similar to those of Sydney.

excerpts.text:
The estimated resident population (ERP) is the official measure of Australia's population based on the concept of usual residence. It includes all people, regardless of nationality or citizenship, who usually live in Australia, except foreign diplomatic personnel and overseas visitors who are in Australia for less than a year or more.

All population data were sourced from the Australian Bureau of Statistics using the most up-to-date estimates available.
